fixes.rationale_full: RFC 9112 §6.1 says an HTTP/1.0 message carrying Transfer-Encoding has faulty framing even if Content-Length is present, and §6.3 then requires a proxy to discard the response with a 502. ResponseParser.status() already accepts only HTTP/1.<digit>, but the parser threw away the minor version. ResponseParser.Head (package-private, not public API) now records http10 = statusLine.charAt(7)=='0', taken when the final head is built. framing() keeps the RFC 9112 §6.3 order: HEAD, 204 and 304 are still bodyless first, so they never become INVALID_RESPONSE because of framing headers (FR-PROXY-014 AC-6). Next, a non-empty Transfer-Encoding list on an HTTP/1.0 head throws invalid("Transfer-Encoding on an HTTP/1.0 response"), which is ProxyException INVALID_RESPONSE and a 502, before the CL+TE check and the chunked check run. HTTP/1.0 responses without Transfer-Encoding are unchanged: Content-Length works (the existing AC-1 test with HTTP/1.0 599) and read-until-close works (new guard test). Annotated // @req SEC-PROXY-004.
